predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire
predecessors.text: Louis II's share of the 1255 partition, 'the Palatinate and Upper Bavaria' (Louis the Strict page)

successors.name: Kingdom of Bavaria
successors.text: 'The electorate existed until 1806, when Bavaria was proclaimed a kingdom' (Electorate of Bavaria page)

ledger.x: 1260: the Duchy of Bavaria enters the map as Louis II's Upper Bavaria with the Palatinate, after the partition of 1255.
1268: Louis II inherits part of the Hohenstaufen lands.
1329: the Treaty of Pavia gives the Palatinates away.
1340: Louis IV reunites Bavaria.
ledger.cpn: Duchy of Lower Bavaria (House of Wittelsbach)

ledger.x: 1342: Tyrol passes to the Wittelsbach.

1349: the Wittelsbach possessions are divided again, 'after Günther's early death in 1349 and divided the Wittelsbach possessions among themselves again' (the sentence's subject is cut off in the extract read; it follows the account of Louis IV's sons).
1353: Bavaria-Landshut is created.
1363: Tyrol goes to the Habsburgs.

1392: 'in 1392 Bavaria-Landshut was divided for the three dukes and so Bavaria-Munich and Bavaria-Ingolstadt were split off' (Landshut page); 'Four Duchies existed after the division of 1392' (Duchy of Bavaria page).

1429: the Straubing inheritance is divided 'under arbitration of the emperor' among Bavaria-Munich, Bavaria-Landshut and Bavaria-Ingolstadt (Straubing page); 'In 1429 parts of Bavaria-Straubing were united with Bavaria-Landshut' (Landshut page).
1447: Bavaria-Landshut annexes Bavaria-Ingolstadt (infobox 'Annexed Bavaria-Ingolstadt: 1447').
1503: the Landshut inheritance is fought over.
1505: arbitration ends the war.
1505: Bavaria is reunited under the Munich line.
1505: Palatinate-Neuburg is carved out.
1505: Maximilian I takes the Tyrolean offices.
1623: Maximilian receives the Upper Palatinate.
1623: the Duchy becomes an Electorate.
1632: the Swedes occupy Munich.
1635: the Swedish occupation ends.
1702: a western strip joins Bavaria in Cliopatria's outline.
1704: Austria occupies Bavaria after Blenheim.
1706: the western strip leaves the outline.
1714: Bavaria is restored.
1741: Charles Albert overruns Upper Austria and Bohemia.
1742: Austria overruns Bavaria.
1742: Bohemia is lost.
1744: Charles VII is back in Munich.
1777: the Bavarian Wittelsbach line dies out and the Palatinate, Jülich and Berg join Bavaria.
1778: Lower Bavaria is claimed by Austria.
1779: Teschen ends the dispute.
1779: the Innviertel goes to Austria.
1792: France overruns the Palatinate.
1801: the occupation ends in cession.
1801: Lunéville.
1803: Bavaria receives the Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg.
1803: Bavaria receives the Prince-Bishopric of Bamberg.
1803: Bavaria receives the Prince-Bishopric of Freising.
1803: Bavaria receives the Prince-Bishopric of Augsburg.
1803: Bavaria receives the Prince-Bishopric of Passau (in part).
1805: Tyrol and Vorarlberg come to Bavaria.
1805: Augsburg.
1805: the last year of the electorate.

wars.name: War of the Succession of Landshut
wars.outcome: Arbitration by Emperor Maximilian I on 30 July 1505 at the Diet of Cologne: the Munich line kept the rest, the Palatine heirs got Palatinate-Neuburg, Maximilian took Kufstein, Rattenberg, Kitzbühel and other places, and Nuremberg gained Lauf, Hersbruck and…

wars.name: Thirty Years' War
wars.outcome: Maximilian kept the electoral dignity and the Upper Palatinate at the Peace of Westphalia in 1648 and gave up the Lower Palatinate; the Swedes occupied Munich in 1632, and the French and Swedes ravaged the land after the Truce of Ulm of 1647 was broken.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: Defeat at Blenheim on 13 August 1704, the imperial ban (1706) and Austrian occupation, and restoration at the Treaty of Baden in 1714.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession
wars.outcome: Charles Albert took Prague (November 1741), was crowned king of Bohemia (19 December 1741) and emperor (12 February 1742); Bohemia was lost in December 1742 and Bavaria occupied; he regained Munich in October 1744; the Treaty of Füssen of 22 April 1745…

wars.name: War of the Bavarian Succession
wars.outcome: Treaty of Teschen, 13 May 1779: Austria kept the Innviertel and returned Lower Bavaria to Charles Theodore.

wars.name: French Revolutionary Wars
wars.outcome: France overran the Palatinate in 1792, invaded Bavaria in 1795-1796 (armistice of 7 September 1796), and at Lunéville on 9 February 1801 Bavaria lost the Palatinate, Zweibrücken and Jülich.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.outcome: Peace of Pressburg of 26 December 1805: Bavaria received Tyrol and Vorarlberg and Austria recognised the royal titles of Bavaria and Württemberg.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated on the pages opened for these years: partitions among the dynasty's lines, scattered possessions (Tyrol, the Dutch counties) and outlines drawn by Cliopatria; the Palatinates in 1329, the Landshut…

Treaty lines: Teschen (13 May 1779) fixes the Innviertel frontier, Lunéville (9 February 1801) the left-bank cession, the Final Recess (25 February 1803) the bishoprics, Pressburg (26 December 1805) Tyrol and Vorarlberg.
